messages:
sara_infra: quick heads-up — euc2-gpu cluster seeing a sharp NCCL bandwidth collapse after last night's infra push. noticed across 4 racks. @oliver_net can you take a look?

oliver_net: on it. which kernel/ofed combo did we roll?

sara_infra: rolled kernel 6.1.24 + OFED 6.1.2 + updated mlx firmware 22.8. Packet coalescing flags were enabled by default in that firmware.

max_gpu: observed training jobs drop from ~85GB/s to ~12GB/s between pods on same hostgroup. latency spikes and retries in NCCL.

lili_sre: opened an incident and pinned affected hosts: euc2-rack-17..20. Incident ID INC-2026-342.

raj_telemetry: sending short telemetry dump: spotted NCCL log lines showing transport fallback. snippet: ```NCCL INFO topology: using net/net for rank 2 pair (ib0->ib1)
NCCL WARN transport 'ib' returned -1, falling back to 'sock'
```

oliver_net: that matches. if firmware turned on large coalescing, it's causing packets to be buffered and reordered; IB/EFA QP timeouts then trigger retries and NCCL falls back. Can we repro with ib_read_bw?

max_gpu: ran ib_read_bw between nodes in same rack — it reports ~60Gb/s when targeted but fluctuates wildly and shows TCP retransmissions at kernel level. `ethtool -S mlx5_core` shows high `rx_discard` counts.

raj_telemetry: attaching small command output (trimmed): ```# ibv_devinfo -v
node GUID: 0x1a2b3c4d5e6f
link_layer: InfiniBand
max_mr_size: 0x7fffffff
``` and ```# ethtool -S ens6f0 | grep rx_discard
rx_discard: 4821
```

oliver_net: try toggling NIC coalesce sysfs flags on one host for quick test: `echo 0 > /sys/module/mlx5_core/parameters/flush_*` (example) or disable GRO/GSO/TCP segmentation offloads as trial.

sara_infra: rolled a quick change on one node (euc2-r17n3) — disabled GRO/TX with `ethtool -K ens6f0 gro off gso off tso off`. Starting a synthetic NCCL all-reduce.

max_gpu: initial run shows immediate improvement: aggregate bandwidth to ~78GB/s on that node pair. Other nodes still bad.

lili_sre: can we quick-validate rollback plan? If firmware is culprit, full rollback is heavy. Could we patch OFED config to keep coalescing off cluster-wide until vendor fixes?

oliver_net: vendor recommends firmware rollback or setting ``mlx5_core.pm_rq_flags=0x0`` on kernel cmdline to disable wqe coalescing. Also suggested `rdma_ucm` minor patch.

deploy-bot: deploy job 95231 started: rolling kernel-params change to euc2-rack-17 (batch size 4).

raj_telemetry: pushed cluster-wide alert rule to detect NCCL fallback lines and rx_discard > 1000.

max_gpu: scheduling cross-rack tests tomorrow AM once we have patch rolled. will document perf deltas.

sara_infra: thanks. please prioritize rollback on prod-critical training pools if degraded >50% for 1h.

oliver_net: note: timeline for vendor firmware rollback ETA 48-72h if we escalate. Meanwhile kernel-arg toggle is quick but requires reboot.

lili_sre: created runbook note in INC-2026-342 channel with commands we used. adding vendor contacts and escalation steps.

max_gpu: adding test scripts to repo: `tools/inf-bench/ib_nccl_test.sh` — will push after sanity run.

raj_telemetry: also saw increased kernel `rq_timeout` logs on affected hosts: `mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: QP 5123 RQ timeout`.

oliver_net: recommend we tag affected hosts in inventory and exclude them from autoscaler pools until fixed to avoid hitting degraded nodes.

sara_infra: agreed. will patch autoscaler to exclude tag `euc2-mlx5-degraded` and remove after remediation.

lili_sre: incident updated, setting P2. will reconvene 0900 UTC.

sara_infra: final note: if anyone sees similar in other regions (I think west-us saw a different OFED minor bump last week), pls post infra details (kernel/ofed/fw) so we can correlate. thanks!
